title: Seasons and school years
skills: Describe routines with he and she
goal: Compare school years and write two routine sentences.
reading_task: Work in pairs: each pair reads one place and finds the start, end and summer holiday. Share the facts, then compare Japan with a US place.
grammar_task: Use I/they + verb and he/she + verb-s. Work on the rules and two question pairs; finish the remaining practice at home.
writing_task: Answer the two calendar questions and write two sentences with begins or ends. In the final four minutes, explain Japan’s summer break.
prep: Name the four seasons and think about your school year.
home: Read the complete main text with audio. Check the facts collected in class.
Practise the remaining affirmative examples and question pairs, slides 7–27.
Answer Part C on workbook page 3 and improve your two comparison sentences.
check: Check the country fact and third-person ending separately. Japan’s summer break is inside its school year.
support: Assign one place per pair before sharing the whole comparison. Use starts / ends / summer holiday as prompts.
exit: Explain one calendar difference without copying a whole sentence.

title: WhatsApp from Argentina: routines
goal: Describe Carlito’s routine and explain what he does and does not do.
reading_task: Read Carlito’s message. Find who travels with him and how far they travel. Compare his journey with yours.
grammar_task: Practise do not / does not + the base verb. Contrast an action with be. Try two question pairs before checking.
writing_task: Answer the message questions orally. Write two facts about Carlito and one true negative about your journey. Use the final four minutes to check does not + base verb.
prep: Bring your calendar answers and vocabulary notes.
Prepare one sentence about how you get to school.
home: Replay the horse message. Answer the workbook page 2 questions in writing.
Use Writing sheet Part A: write your routine, a friend’s routine and one negative.
check: Require the correct negative meaning and base verb; does not rides is not correct.
support: Say I ride → he rides → he does not ride. Then ask for a different example.
exit: Write one true does not sentence without a model.

title: Email from India: questions and teamwork
skills: Give short answers and report a partner’s answer
goal: Explain how Samuel travels and ask a partner about a routine.
reading_task: Read Samuel’s email. Find how his brothers help and how far they travel. Explain each answer using a detail from the message.
grammar_task: Build do/does questions and short answers. Reorder a question and ask it before checking the answer.
writing_task: Write two questions for a partner and record the answers. Use the final four minutes to correct one question independently.
prep: Bring your negative sentences and vocabulary notes.
Think of a question you want to ask about someone’s journey.
home: Replay the email and finish the reading questions on workbook page 4.
Finish the do/does practice and short answers, slides 1–17.
Write three questions and short answers in Writing sheet Part B.
check: Questions need the correct auxiliary and base verb. Check meaning before spelling.
support: Rehearse a short answer orally, then write it. Refer to Samuel’s documented routine, not a claim about his life today.
exit: Write and answer a new Does ...? question.

title: Instagram from the islands: listen and reply
skills: Listen for the main idea and details
goal: Understand the boat journey and begin a reply to one of the three messages.
reading_task: Listen twice before opening the post. Answer the three listening questions, then read the message to check your evidence.
grammar_task: Use where/when/how and frequency words. Select one example per rule and two checks. Practise common stative verbs in the summary.
writing_task: Choose a sender, plan and start a 50–70-word reply. Answer the sender’s question. Use the final four minutes to check one question and one frequency sentence; finish the reply at home.
prep: Bring your questions, answers and vocabulary notes.
Think about travelling by boat. Keep the Instagram message closed until after listening.
home: Replay the boat recording and finish workbook page 5.
Finish the information-question and frequency practice, slides 18–43.
Finish and improve the 50–70-word reply on workbook page 6. Read it aloud and correct two sentences.
check: Look for another island, five minutes and walking after the boat. A reply must address its reader’s question.
support: Allow replay at the learner’s speed. Provide a writing plan, then let the learner draft independently.
exit: Name one point to review before the exam on 12 November.
